memory: I tested a radius‑matched silicone annular shim: inner radius 0.33 mm, thickness 0.06 mm, Shore A10, cured 24 h. At 3.00 N and bench 21.1°C, profilometry peak‑to‑valley rim depression = 1.8 ±0.5 μm; τ deviation from Rc–linear trend = 2.7% (within 3%). Shim compressed 0.028 mm under preload; sensitivity: misalignment >0.03 mm or precompression >0.04 mm reintroduces rim strain. Correction upheld: rigid spacer edge caused prior τ overshoot; this softer, thinner shim restores τ but narrows alignment/compression tolerances. Current position: map allowable precompression and alignment windows across thickness/hardness sweep.
openQuestion: What maximum preload-induced precompression (mm) for the 0.06 mm A10 shim keeps rim depression ≤2 μm and τ within 3%?
